question: Compare the quantitative triggers in the four-leg All-Way Stop crash warrant and the 8-hour volume warrant.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Both warrants are permissive (Option) criteria for installing all-way stop control based on an engineering study, but they use different metrics. The crash warrant for a four-leg intersection is triggered by five or more reported correctable crashes in 12 months, or six or more in 36 months. The 8-hour volume warrant is triggered by combined vehicle/bicycle/pedestrian entering volumes of at least 300 units per hour on the major-street approaches and at least 200 units per hour on the minor-street approaches, sustained for each of the same 8 hours of a typical day. Options (permitted): - Crash warrant (four-leg): All-way stop control may be installed where an engineering study indicates "there are five or more reported crashes in a 12-month period or six or more reported crashes in a 36-month period that were of a type susceptible to correction by the installation of all-way stop control." (By comparison, the three-leg thresholds are four crashes in 12 months or five in 36 months.) - 8-hour volume warrant: All-way stop control may be installed where an engineering study indicates (A) "the combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering the intersection from the major-street approaches is at least 300 units per hour for each of any 8 hours of a typical day" and (B) "the combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering the intersection from the minor-street approaches is at least 200 units per hour for each of any of the same 8 hours." - Key comparison: the crash warrant counts discrete safety events over long observation windows (12 or 36 months) limited to crash types correctable by all-way stop control, while the volume warrant counts multimodal demand (vehicles + bicycles + pedestrians combined) that must be met simultaneously on major and minor streets during the same 8 hours of a single typical day. Citations: - Section 2B.13 Option §1 (p.79) - Section 2B.16 Option §1 (p.79)
gold_answer: The crash warrant may apply with at least 5 correctable crashes in 12 months or 6 in 36 months. The volume warrant may apply when, for the same 8 hours, major-street entering volume is at least 300 units/hour and minor-street entering volume at least 200 units/hour, with a possible 70-percent adjustment if major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph.
